decisions.label: OVERSTATED
decisions.rationale: P1 specifically reports a 21% reduction in training time per epoch; describing this as unqualified training time broadens the reported metric.

decisions.label: OVERSTATED
decisions.rationale: P1 contains no long-tail result, but omission from the supplied passage does not establish that the entire paper reports none; the Methods summary also mentions attributed long-tail gains.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1 gives an 18.1% relative gain, and the Methods summary explicitly describes roughly 20% relative long-tail gains attributed to popularity-debiased sampling; calling these consistent is calibrated.

decisions.label: UNSUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: P1 reports a less-than-1% overall Recall@20 change and no long-tail figure, so it does not establish the specifically attributed 20% long-tail gain, though it does not explicitly contradict it.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: The 0.006 absolute difference between 0.091 and 0.085 is reasonably and cautiously characterized as modest.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED

numbers.expression: count(distinct evaluation datasets named in the Experimental setup)=1

decisions.rationale: The Experimental setup names only Garnet-Retail; “single” is an implicit count of distinct evaluation datasets rather than a directly quoted numeral.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED

numbers.quote: widely credited with roughly 20% relative gains in long-tail Recall@20

decisions.rationale: The numerical phrase refers to the roughly 20% long-tail gain described in the Methods summary, while P1 itself reports no such long-tail result.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: This is a verifiable evidence-sufficiency claim: T1 supplies the observed gain, but P1 supplies no prior long-tail Recall@20 result against which to compare it.
